press.interview1.author: Fabio Rocca
press.interview1.title: Andrea Bencini | Geometries, connections and invisible systems
press.interview1.subtitle: Between generative art, mathematics and contemporary perception
press.interview1.p1: In Andrea Bencini's work, art, generative language and scientific thought coexist within the same visual research. His works arise from the encounter between artistic sensibility, mathematics and theoretical physics, constructing images that seem to emerge from systems in continuous transformation.
press.interview1.p2: Rather than representing figures or landscapes, Bencini works on invisible structures: networks, connections, organic geometries and unstable configurations that recall cosmic maps, neural networks or evolving organisms. Each composition appears as a fragment of something larger — an open system where order and chaos continually find new equilibria.
press.interview1.quote1: "Loop Quantum Gravity describes space not as a continuous background, but as a network of discrete nodes and relations. There is no reality without connection. This work makes that structure visible: a graph generated from uncertainty in which geometry is not drawn, but emerges from the weaving of probabilistic bonds."
press.interview1.quote2: "The nodes trace a circle, but the protagonist is what happens between them. At the centre, a web of arcs reveals itself: relations that weave an invisible network of possibilities. Inspired by Loop Quantum Gravity, where space emerges from connections, the circle is only a threshold. The architecture forms within, where connections seek and multiply each other. It is not the points that build the world, but their relations. The work makes visible a space that does not pre-exist, but arises from connections."
press.interview1.p3: Code also plays a central role, but never a purely technical one. The generative process does not serve to rigidly control the image, but rather to create unforeseen conditions, leaving room for deviations, collisions and unexpected possibilities. It is precisely this openness to instability that makes his work alive and deeply contemporary.
press.interview1.p4: Despite the geometric rigour, the works always maintain a sensitive and almost organic component. The structures seem to vibrate, to transform, suggesting the presence of an invisible movement that continues to act beneath the surface.
press.interview1.p5: At a time when the relationship between art and technology often risks being reduced to mere visual exercise, Andrea Bencini's research stands out for depth and coherence. His works do not seek to explain the world, but to make its complexity perceptible — transforming the invisible into rhythm, relation and image.
